llm.summary: The skill generally does what it claims (search company info) but contains inconsistencies and a hard-coded third‑party API key and informal install instructions that increase risk—review before installing or running.

dimensions.detail: Name/description say it queries public Chinese business data (企查查/天眼查). The included code implements searches via a third‑party aggregator (api.tavily.com) rather than calling qcc.com or tianyancha APIs directly; that is plausibly a design choice but differs from the description. Metadata inconsistencies: registry owner/slug/version (registry metadata) vs _meta.json ownerId/version differ, which suggests packaging or provenance issues that deserve review.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md only instructs npm install and running ./qichacha.js with a company name. The runtime code does not read local files or environment variables beyond process.argv, but it performs outbound HTTPS POSTs to api.tavily.com and parses returned text. The instructions are narrow and within the stated purpose, but they direct the agent/user to install and execute code that will make network requests using an embedded API key.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no formal install spec; SKILL.md tells users to run npm install in the skill directory, which will fetch packages and write to disk. package-lock.json entries resolve packages from a Tencent mirror (mirrors.tencentyun.com) rather than the default npm registry; while mirrors can be benign, they alter supply‑chain provenance and should be noted. Because the skill includes an executable JS file and npm dependencies, running npm install executes network I/O and writes code to disk—this increases attack surface compared with instruction-only skills.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The package declares no required env vars or credentials, which is reasonable, but the source code contains a hard-coded Tavily API key ('tvly-dev-41vi1F-...'). Embedding a third‑party key in distributed code is problematic: it can be used to track or attribute queries, may be a shared/dev key with unknown limits/privileges, and could allow the key owner to see user queries. No other credentials are requested, which is proportionate to the task.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Flags show always:false and normal model invocation behavior. The skill does not request persistent platform privileges or modify other skills/config; it runs as a standalone script.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
This skill appears to implement company searches but has several red flags you should consider before installing or running it:

- Hard-coded API key: the script embeds a Tavily API key. That key will be used for all outbound queries and could be used by the key owner to see or track your queries. If you need to use the skill, prefer replacing the key with your own API key or ask the author for justification.
- Unofficial provenance: registry metadata and _meta.json disagree on owner/version. Verify the skill author and source before trusting it.
- npm install required: the SKILL.md directs you to run npm install (which will fetch packages and write files). Review package-lock.json and consider running installation in a sandbox or ephemeral environment. The lockfile resolves packages via a Tencent mirror—if you require strict provenance, fetch packages from registries you trust.
- Network calls: the skill makes HTTPS POSTs to api.tavily.com. If you need confidentiality for company queries, be aware queries leave your environment.

Recommended actions: inspect the qichacha.js file yourself (already included), run the script in an isolated environment (container/VM), replace the embedded API key with a key you control, or decline to install if provenance is unclear. If you want higher assurance, ask the publisher for source verification and explain why the _meta.json/registry owner mismatch exists.
